text:
elena: Quick sync — we're planning to remove the legacy default model alias (the implicit "compat-model") on Nov 15. Need guidance on client SDK behavior so we don't silently break PLG apps. Options I see:
  • (a) SDK auto-pin to last-successful model id + send `X-Client-Pinned` header, warn in logs.
  • (b) SDK leave requests unpinned and surface 4xx to apps so they must opt in.
  • (c) server-side soft-fallback to nearest compatible variant (quantized/etc).
Which approach balances stability + explicitness? cc @matt @sam @vivek

matt: leaning (a) but only if the SDK also emits a clear warning and telemetry. PLG users expect continuity; surprise errors are worse. SDK should set an opt-out flag.

sam: agree with (a) + admin controls. Also: we need a 30d deprecation notice for Dedicated customers and a toggle in the console to opt their org out during rollout.

vivek: +1 on explicitness. Also call out response-shape changes separately — if we change fields we must version the response (e.g., `X-Response-Version`) and return 406/409 for incompatible combos. For alias removal alone, pinning is fine but doc it.

elena: thanks. Implementation ask: @matt can you add the `X-Client-Pinned` header in the SDK PR and a metric `sdk.pinned_autopin`? Example client snippet we can show in docs:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Accept-Model: redwood/gpt-3.2" 
  -H "X-Client-Pinned: gpt-3.2@20230901" 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
The SDK should also log a single warning on startup when it auto-pins.

matt: will open the SDK PR today. I'll implement header + metric + a `REDWOOD_AUTO_PIN=false` env opt-out. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

deploy-bot: CI: starting deploy for `sdk/clients#432` -> staging. Tests: running.

sam: I'll draft the deprecation note + sample migration snippets for both REST and our JS/Go SDKs. Assigning to @elena for review. Target publish: Nov 1.

elena: one more question — should the server treat `Accept-Model: *` as "prefer latest compatible" or treat it as ambiguous legacy behavior and reject? My vote: reject with 409 and a helpful body suggesting an explicit model header.

vivek: agree. `*` is too ambiguous. Reject and include example `Accept-Model` value and link to migration docs.

docs-bot: PR created: `infra/docs#987` "Model pinning and Accept-Model semantics" — reviewers: sam, elena.

elena: Action items recap: matt — SDK header + metric + opt-out; sam — docs draft + examples; vivek — spec for 406/409 response behavior; elena — changelog + comms. Ping here when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
